raw.assessment: The incumbent is adequate for many routine exports: 32/40 had the intended courses, and unchanged-assignment centers had seven-minute median handling. Failures cluster around assignment changes, supporting—but not establishing—a mismatch between current service state and requested-week expectations. Renamed courses in two affected exports limit an assignment-only account: identity matching or timetable disagreement could also matter. The 17-minute overall median and 80% course-set accuracy miss the targets. Zero observed cross-center rows is bounded evidence; the split-course center was absent. Fast execution alongside long replacement waits suggests an operational delay, but elapsed waiting is not measured active handling. All evidence is stipulated synthetic data.

openings.claim: Requested-week course membership may be distorted by applying current instructor assignments; renames may separately create apparent omissions when coordinators compare names.
openings.delta: Distinguishes missing course identities from present courses carrying unexpected names before choosing an export correction.
openings.prediction: With intended course identities held fixed, assignment changes will alter exported membership if the temporal hypothesis holds. Rename-only changes will preserve membership but may trigger coordinator mismatch reports.
openings.probe: In fabricated staging, replay unchanged, assignment-change, rename-only and split-course examples. Record exported identities and names; have consenting coordinators identify the intended weekly set. Verify center boundaries and concurrent attendance entry. Reserve the documented CSV unchanged; time-box investigation within six engineer-days and existing hosting.
assumptions: Intended weekly membership can be agreed; historical state availability remains unknown.

openings.claim: Would faster replacement availability materially reduce coordinator handling, or does checking and importing dominate active work?
openings.delta: Separates queue delay from the handling-time success measure.
openings.prediction: A replacement bottleneck will produce repeated request/status work; a checking/import bottleneck will leave substantial active work even when a corrected file is immediately available.
openings.probe: Use the two short sessions per consenting coordinator with fabricated files: counterbalance immediate replacement against the usual request process, timing checking, requesting, downloading and importing separately from waiting.
assumptions: A usability result would guide a bounded change, not establish success across the next 40 exports.

raw.assessment: Assignment changes and renames are associated with affected exports, but their causal role is unproved. Replacement delay and active handling also need separate measurement. Both openings retain private processing, the documented CSV, concurrent attendance entry, and the six-day/hosting ceiling.

openings.claim: Selecting courses through their relationship to the requested week could prevent omissions associated with using current instructor assignments.
openings.delta: Change the temporal representation from current assignment to center-course-week membership. Recompose the export by selecting authorized membership tuples, then joining attendance by stable course identity and emitting the existing CSV schema.
openings.prediction: If current-assignment selection causes omissions, an instructor handoff will change the incumbent course set but leave a correctly specified week-membership selection intact. Unchanged-assignment controls should agree.
openings.probe: In private staging, compare both selectors on fabricated handoffs, renames, and a split, including identical labels across centers and attendance entered during export. Compare stable IDs against coordinator-approved intended sets. Bound implementation to six engineer-days and existing hosting; proceed only if trustworthy membership history is available.
assumptions: Stable course identities and usable historical membership can be obtained within the budget.
Coordinators can resolve which split courses belong to a requested week.

openings.claim: Does a replacement cycle consume active coordinator effort, or mainly introduce elapsed waiting?
openings.delta: Represent each export as a handling trajectory. Recompose per-export handling time by summing active intervals for checking, requesting, downloading, correcting, and importing; record waiting separately.
openings.prediction: Waiting-dominated cycles would show long request-to-delivery gaps but little active replacement work; reconciliation-dominated cycles would show repeated schedule comparisons or spreadsheet corrections.
openings.probe: Use the six coordinators' two sessions with fabricated normal and affected exports to observe these intervals. If active replacement work dominates, test an authorized in-service rerun control; if comparison dominates, prioritize course-selection correction. Recheck the next 40 exports against all three success measures.
assumptions: Reduced waiting alone does not establish reduced handling time.

openings.claim: Current assignments may distort weekly membership; renames may separately cause name mismatches or timetable disagreement.
openings.discriminator: With intended IDs fixed, handoffs alter incumbent membership; rename-only cases retain IDs despite reported omissions.
openings.fit: Probes preserve C1–C4; implementation depends on history and six-day/hosting feasibility.
openings.probe: Privately compare incumbent and authorized center-course-week selection joined to attendance by stable ID, emitting unchanged CSV. Replay fabricated controls, handoffs, renames, splits and identical cross-center labels; agree intended sets with coordinators; verify boundaries and concurrent attendance entry.
openings.uncertainty: Causality unproved; stable IDs, trustworthy history, split membership and timetable completeness/update timing unresolved.

openings.claim: Replacement waiting may contribute little active handling; checking or importing may dominate.
openings.discriminator: Repeated request/status work versus schedule comparisons, corrections or import effort when replacements are immediate.
openings.fit: Preserves private processing, CSV, concurrent entry and six-day/hosting limits.
openings.probe: Six coordinators, two sessions each: fabricated normal/affected files; counterbalance immediate replacement versus usual requests. Time checking, requesting, correcting, downloading and importing separately from waiting. Test authorized in-service rerun if replacement work dominates; prioritize selection correction if comparison dominates.
openings.uncertainty: Sessions may not represent weekly work; shorter waiting alone proves no handling improvement.

post_distill.decision: Probe both before choosing a change. Synthetic baseline: 80% intended sets, 17-minute median; zero sampled leaks excludes split-center coverage. Validate next 40: median ≤12 minutes, ≥95% intended sets, zero cross-center records.
